html:
SMTO-UI-0016 — A login field set to Number needs a number

GUID: 7896f010-3b15-4480-b582-ae142d88e2b2
Slug: ui-login-number-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • One extra login field is set to hold a number, but its value is empty or isn't a usable number. The connection wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store, open this connection, then Advanced login settings. Find the Login field row whose Value type is number. Only rows set to number are checked this way, so that's where the problem is.
  2. Enter a plain number in its Value box, such as 1 or 30, without words, spaces or symbols. An empty box or text like 'yes' can't be sent as a number.
  3. If the value isn't really a number, change its Value type to string instead, then select Save. The value type has to match what the website's login form expects.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without this message.

If it still fails

  • Check the website's login documentation for what this field should contain, or send the copied error details to the person who manages this connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An additional session-login field with Value type number is blank or does not convert to a finite JavaScript number.

What this means

  • An additional login field marked numeric is blank or converts to a non-finite number. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • An additional login field marked numeric is blank or converts to a non-finite number.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the marked field's type and numeric format without logging credentials.

How to fix it

  • sessionEditor() in http_profile_editor.js rejects a Login field row of kind number when its value is blank or Number(value) is not finite. Enter a finite numeric value, or change the row's Value type to match the data the login endpoint expects.
  • Enter a finite numeric value for the indicated login field.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The field contains a finite intended number.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
